summary: Fumio Matsuda works in religious and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Komazawa University and served as an executive committee chair for the Association for the Study of Indian Religions in 1997.

Fumio Ouchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He earned his doctorate at Otani University, where he served as an assistant professor (~1990–2000) and later as a professor (~2000–2013).

Fumio Shoji specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Rissho University (~1998–2007), where he later served as an assistant professor in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (~2013–2018).
Fumio Tamamuro specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Meiji University (~1954–1963) and later taught there (~1970–2006).

Futoshi Omae is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He was a lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 1990–1991) and held posts at Shimane Prefectural Junior College of International Studies (1997) and Shimane International Junior College (1998).

Futoshi Takehashi specializes in Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at Otani University (attested 1992) and served as an assistant at the Institute of Shin Buddhist Studies from 1995 to 1997.

Fyodor Buslaev worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the Faculty of History and Philology of Moscow University (~1834–1838) and held a post at Moscow State University in 1846.

Fyodor Shcherbatskoy specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Saint Petersburg and under Bühler, Minaev, Oldenburg, and Jacobi. He served as a professor at the University of Saint Petersburg (~1900–1941).

Félix Nève was an Indologist and linguist. He earned his doctorate at KU Leuven (~1835–1838) and studied under Christian Lassen, Friedrich Wilhelm Thiersch, and Eugène Burnouf. He became a professor at KU Leuven in 1841.
G. Srinivasa Murti worked in Indology and other fields. He served as Director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1938–1949 and 1971).

G. Thomas Tanselle studied at Yale University. He held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1960–1978), the John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation (1978–2006), and Columbia University (~1978–2004), and served as president of the Bibliographical Society of America.
G. V. Aston specializes in philosophy and religious studies. Aston earned a PhD in philosophy at the University of Canterbury (1986–2004), where he studied under Paul Harrison.

G. V. Srinivasa Rao worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Senior Epigraphical Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India until 1945 and retired from the Government Epigraphist for India.

id: P:Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso
summary: Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso studied under Tenzin Gyatso and Trijang Rinpoche.

Gadjin M. Nagao specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University under Ryotai Hatani and Susumu Yamaguchi, and later served as Chair of Buddhist Studies at Kyoto University (1935–1971).
Gail Hinich Sutherland works in religious studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Chicago under Carol Bolon and Wendy Doniger, and also studied under Virendra Singh.

Gajanan Balkrishna Palsule worked in Indology and linguistics. He was a sub-editor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1957) and held a post at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1968–1981).

Galmangoda Sumanapala specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has served as a Senior Professor and as Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies at the University of Kelaniya (attested 2007, 2012).

Galsang Gomboev worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski and taught Mongolian at the University of Saint Petersburg from 1855 to 1863.

Gananath Obeyesekere is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Peradeniya and University of Washington, and held faculty posts at the University of Ceylon, UC San Diego, and Princeton University (1980–2000).
